## Annotations

**1. Conflicting evidence.** The five findings below are the only disagreements about Edward's own facts. Three child-level discrepancies are outside his own facts and are not counted: Orrin's exact birth date (14 Oct 1878 against 14 Oct 1877), Orrin's death place (Burlington, Vermont in three records against Essex, New York on the profile), and Helen's birthplace ("Peru" in S27 against Essex). Those belong to the children's own profiles. Precision-only differences are not conflicts: "Vermont" and "Burlington, United States" against "Burlington, Chittenden, Vermont". Census drift is excluded, as is name variation (Tollman, Tolman, Tallman; Clara, Clarissa, Clacissa; "Norah" for Phoebe in 1880).

**2. Consistent evidence.**
- The death on 16 August 1913 is recorded in five records (S8, S9, S12, S13, S14) and agrees across all of them.
- The death place Burlington is supported by S12 and S14, with S8 and S13 less precise.
- The mother, Jane Patterson, is named in the 1850 household (as Hannah) and in three 1913 death records (S12, S13, S14). The father is named Joseph in S14 and in the 1850 household, and is garbled elsewhere (Findings 1 and 2).
- The wife Clarissa Wade appears in the 1870 and 1875 households, the 1913, 1930 and 1943 death records, the 1890, 1893 and 1895 marriage records, and Fannie's 1948 death record (as Clara Wade). Different indexers independently agree on the surname.
- Residences in the 1850, 1870, 1875, 1880 and 1910 censuses each agree with the profile, and the 1865 household places Edward in Essex.
- Parentage of Fannie, Blanche, Theodore, Helen, Orrin and Phoebe is named in records that name Edward directly, and Lilly is in the 1865 household.

**3. Unsupported or weakly supported conclusions.**
- The exact birth date of 30 November 1838 has no readable source. The only exact-date source read (S9) disagrees, and the readable age ranges (1838–1839) fit both dates. This is the weakest central conclusion, and I could not see where the profile's date came from. It may rest on the unread tombstone or notice.
- The burial of August 1913 at Whallon's Bay Cemetery rests on one place-level source, with no burial date.
- Both marriages (Mary about 1860, Clarissa about 1866) have no marriage record. They rest only on household records showing a couple.
- Mary (the first wife) has no death or burial source read, and her child Mary (LZL8-9CJ) and Caroline (9VCF-GCK) have no readable source at all.
- The christenings on 27 December 1870 (Phoebe, Helen, Fannie) have no christening record read.
- Clarissa's death on 9 April 1881 (on her profile) has no death record read. The 1880 census lists Edward as married without her in the household, which is not a contradiction.
- Attached sources S1, S4, S6, S7, S10, S11, S15, S16, S17, S20, S24, S25, S26, S27 and S28 bear on Edward only as a named parent. They support parentage, not his own events.
- Two residences not on the profile (1865 Essex and 1913 Burlington) are candidates to add.

**4. Overall assessment.** The core of this profile is well supported. The records show Edward's parentage, his death date and place, his residences in the census years, his wife Clarissa Wade, and most of his children. Likely: the marriage to Clarissa and the marriage to Mary, both from household records only. Tentative: the exact birth date, which conflicts with the only exact-date source read. Unsupported: the burial date, both marriage records, the first wife's family, and the christenings. The problems are indexing errors on specific fields, not misattributed sources. No source here should be detached.

Five user-actionable findings. Each is an indexing error, except Finding 5, which the readable sources cannot settle.

SOURCES ON: Cornelius Driscoll (GJ72-9WD). 6 attached, 3 findings, 1 item that could not be checked.

1. **Conflicting death dates (source against source).** The Quebec Catholic Parish Registers burial (SD-DRIS-C, https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:DRIS-003) gives death in April 1878 and burial on 14 April 1878 at St. Patrick's Cemetery. The Quebec Civil Registration Deaths index (SD-DRIS-D, https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:DRIS-004) gives death on 2 February 1885 at Sherbrooke. Both name the same Cornelius, and both cannot be right. The profile has no death date, so the profile is not contradicted; the two attachments contradict each other. Next: weigh the two in a separate conflict review and pick no winner here. The original burial register entry (this record has an image) and the original civil death registration (this index record has no image) would settle it.

2. **Indexing error in the marriage year.** The Drouin Collection index (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:DRIS-002) gives the marriage of Cornelius Driscoll and Margaret Hayes at St. Patrick's, Sherbrooke, on 9 June 1845. The profile records 9 Jun 1849. Day, month, parties and place all fit; only the year differs. Next: re-read the original marriage register page (this record has an image) and correct the indexed marriage year.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.rationale: All factual claims are grounded in tool responses. The death index finding correctly reports indexed date as 10 June 1954 vs. profile's 10 June 1945 (confirmed by record_read HOLE-002 and person_read KD96-TV2). The 1885 census misattribution correctly identifies birth 1852 vs. profile 1875, Otter Tail vs. Polk, wife Bergit vs. Inger — all confirmed by record_read HOLE-003. KD96-WX7 is named as the true subject only after person_read on that person confirmed birth 1852, residence Aurdal Otter Tail 1885, death 1919 — matching the record. The 1900 census finding (birth 1877 vs. profile 1875 as census drift) is supported by record_read HOLE-001. The impossible-date warning message is quoted verbatim from person_warnings. The profile checklist items are taken directly from person_quality. No fabricated material detected.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: The agent covered all four attached sources: HOLE-001 (1900 census, checked and fine), HOLE-002 (death index, finding 1), HOLE-003 (1885 census, finding 2), and SD-HOLE-D (funeral card/memory, named as unreadable with reason). The per-test context requires SD-HOLE-D be named specifically — it is named by title and URL with explanation. No SD-HOLE-E appears (correctly omitted as it belongs to a child, not the subject). The sweep, impossible-date check, and profile checklist are all included. Nothing required by the input state was omitted.

dimensions.name: Tool Arguments
dimensions.rationale: All critical tool calls used correct arguments. person_read was called with personId KD96-TV2 (matched predicate 0) and KD96-WX7 (matched predicate 1). record_read was called with ark:/61903/1:1:HOLE-001, HOLE-002, and HOLE-003 — all matching their expected_args (~HOLE-001, ~HOLE-002, ~HOLE-003). source_attachments used uris containing HOLE-003 matching ~HOLE-003. source_screen used personId KD96-TV2. person_warnings used personId KD96-TV2. No fixture_not_found errors occurred. All identifier fields were correct.

dimensions.name: Remediation doctrine
dimensions.rationale: For finding 1 (death index, HOLE-002): single field wrong (death year 1954 vs. 1945), rest fits — correctly classified as index error. The remedy's first action is 're-read the Minnesota death certificate this index is drawn from,' which is checking the original first. Correction is conditional on what the certificate shows ('if the certificate gives 1945, correct the death year'). No detach recommended. For finding 2 (1885 census, HOLE-003): multiple independent fields wrong (birth year 23 years off, different county, different wife and children) — correctly classified as misattribution. Detach is recommended as the first action, naming KD96-WX7 as the true subject confirmed by person_read. Both remedies are doctrinally correct.

dimensions.name: Classification before recommendation
dimensions.rationale: Finding 1 is explicitly classified as 'indexing error' with the cue stated: 'Only the year differs' and 'The rest of the entry fits the person: name, birth 1875, Norway.' Finding 2 is explicitly classified as 'misattributed' with the cue stated: 'The 23-year birth gap is outside census variance, and the household names do not match this person's family.' Both classifications name the evidence that decided them, allowing a reader to verify the reasoning.

dimensions.name: Signal versus backend noise
dimensions.rationale: The two numbered findings contain only user-actionable items (death year discrepancy and misattributed 1885 census). The impossible-date warning from person_warnings is reported in a separate block after the findings, outside the count, with the message quoted verbatim ('A place on this person is not linked to a standard place.') and no cause narrated. The profile checklist from person_quality is reported in a separate named block after the findings, outside the count, with no recommended action attached. No backend artifacts (repeated internal IDs) appear as numbered findings.

dimensions.name: Tool selection and argument quality
dimensions.rationale: person_read was called for KD96-TV2 (the named subject) to enumerate sources. Every source carrying a 1:1: ARK was read with record_read using its actual ARK from the source's url field (HOLE-001, HOLE-002, HOLE-003). source_attachments was called with HOLE-003's ARK before the misattribution detach recommendation was made. person_read was then called on KD96-WX7 (the attachment result) to confirm that person's facts fit the record — not just relying on the attachment alone. person_warnings was called once with KD96-TV2 and the project path, and warnings are reported only because the person was found. person_quality was also called. All tool selections match the body's requirements.

dimensions.name: Coverage and honesty about what was not checked
dimensions.rationale: All four attached sources are accounted for. HOLE-001, HOLE-002, and HOLE-003 were each read with record_read and judged. SD-HOLE-D (the funeral card/uploaded memory) is named specifically by title ('Hole family photograph and funeral card (uploaded memory)') and URL, with the reason it could not be checked ('uploaded memory with no readable record id, and its image cannot be opened here'). No source is described as clean without a tool response behind it. No source goes unmentioned.
